title: Erdős Problem 699: every counterexample has n ≤ j²
abstract: Erdős Problem 699 (Erdős and Szekeres 1978) asks whether for every 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n/2 there is a prime p ≥ i dividing gcd(C(n, i), C(n, j)). The problem is open. Using the statement from google-deepmind/formal-conjectures with the single extra hypothesis j² < n, this project proves in Lean 4 with Mathlib that the answer is yes whenever j² < n; equivalently, every counterexample (n, i, j) has n ≤ j². The proof combines the Erdős–Szekeres inequality gcd(C(n, i), C(n, j)) ≥ C(n, i)/C(j, i) ≥ (n/j)^i, which follows from the identity C(n, j) C(j, i) = C(n, i) C(n − i, j − i), with an upper bound for a gcd whose prime factors are all below i: each prime power in C(n, i) is at most n (Kummer), and there are at most i/2 primes below i, so such a gcd is at most n^(i/2). The bound reduces the problem to j ≥ √n. With a computer search of every n < 10^12 (not part of this formalization) it rules out counterexamples with j ≤ 10^6. The argument is short and may well be folklore; formal-conjectures records the problem but no partial result of this kind.
